trees: Long-billed Corellas feed on the ground in grassy country and nest in old eucalypt hollows. Nests are in hollows of large old eucalypts, sometimes in cavities in gravelly cliffs, on a lining of decayed wood. Around Inverleigh that lines up with River Red Gum and Manna Gum over pasture and Wallaby Grass, and with River Red Gum hollows along the Leigh. No local record names the nest tree.
